hourly.summary: United fans are bracing for a hiding at Anfield in Pochettino's first game, with defensive pessimism so thick you could spread it on toast. One supporter rated the entire backline 'worth -1 goals' while another mused it might be better to miss the match entirely. The only optimism is of the 'sink or swim' variety for young Lacey — classic gallows humour from a fanbase expecting the Reds to paint Anfield red.

daily.summary: Fan sentiment remained in a state of absolute meltdown throughout the day, with both morning and evening summaries scoring a catastrophic 2/10. The mood is defined by relegation-zone panic ahead of an Anfield trip decimated by injuries, fury at a transfer strategy deemed non-existent, and zero faith in the new manager or ownership before a ball is kicked. No shift in sentiment is detectable — only a uniform, rock-bottom despair.

weekly.summary: Fan sentiment began in existential crisis (2/10) with the club in the relegation zone and ownership rage dominant, briefly lifted by Pochettino rumors (4/10) before crashing again on Carrick's sacking (2/10). His appointment brought apprehensive hope (4-5/10) that quickly faded into disillusionment (3/10), finally settling into a dark, resigned acceptance of mediocrity (5/10) laced with gallows humor. The week traces an arc from acute despair through false dawns to cynical resignation, with structural anger at the Glazers/INEOS ownership remaining the constant undercurrent.
